notes.text: Reduce the spacing between tokens in expanded token groups; groups with seven tokens just barely overflow to the right.  Groups with more than seven tokens should wrap; currently, their tokens overflow to the right and are inaccessible.

There is an excessively long delay between sending an action from the dashboard stage queue (e.g. changing an NPC's light mode, or moving them to a new location). Is there any way to speed this up, making the game stage more responsive to changes sent from the dashboard queue?

Please make the opened/expanded group in the NPC Roster more visibly distinct from the other groups -- perhaps by fading out the other groups slightly, or brightening the group that is open, in addition to the pulsing effect.

All player background entries on their in-game character sheets are attempting to display portrait images, despite "No portrait" having been selected in the configuration of the trait; since no portrait art exists, a white box is displayed within the box of every single Advantage displayed on page 3.

The "Refresh UI" button on the Storyteller's debug toolbar doesn't appear to work: A connected client had an overlay image locked as visible and couldn't clear it, but clicking "Refresh UI" didn't do anything.  Refresh UI should trigger a FULL UI rewrite when clicked, just like the staged onboarding process does in its step two.

Please investigate the flow of control for players adding Rouse Dice and triggering Blood Surge themselves during an active roll.  A connected client was unable to activate Blood Surge until he removed a (standard) Rouse Check die from the pool, at which point Blood Surge activated, but he was unable to then add a Rouse Die to the pool.  (Blood Surge rouse dice are to be tracked separately, and shouldn't impede the abiliity of a player to add a normal Rouse Check or Oblivion Rouse Check to a live roll.)

Please review the "PENDING AUTHOR REVIEW.md" document. For each entry, consider whether this is something that can be confirmed with an agent sending commands through the TTS gateway extension. The agent would be encouraged to add any debug tooling or additional architecture (that I would then bake in with a Save & Play) that they need to properly verify the issue. Then, annotate the results of your analysis by adding an emoji to the associated header.  A green circle (🟢) for those issues you're confident can be assessed by an agent; a yellow circle (🟡) for issues that an agent could partially resolve, thus reducing the workload on the human, and a red circle (🔴) for those issues that entirely require a human to test.  For both yellow and red circles, add a note beneath the header explaining your decision, the limitations on what the agent can do, and the specific things the human would still have to validate themselves.
